correctness.rationale: The ordered binary-tree wreath recursion supplies a unique bit at each internal node. The lowest-common-ancestor partition counts each inversion pair exactly once, independently of all other bits; direct/skew sum gives weight 4^(n-j-1). Finite moments follow from two finite geometric sums and were exactly checked. A common infinite-bit coupling gives a deterministic 2^(-n-1) tail, symmetry and Lp convergence. Tail domination proves complete interval support. Selecting Fourier level m-1 with 4^m<=|t|<4^(m+1) forces a cosine factor bounded by cos(1/2)^(2^(m-1)), giving the claimed stretched-exponential characteristic-function bound; Fourier inversion proves C-infinity density. Complete enumeration of 32,768 group elements at n=4 and 359 finite test assertions corroborates the finite formulas without being offered as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Inversions are a canonical global permutation invariant measuring pairwise pivot-reordering discordance. The finding describes a full, compactly supported smooth probability law with nonzero variance at N-squared scale, sharply contrasting classical uniform S_N concentration. The binary-tree group has substantive recent interest in numerical Gaussian elimination. Full interval support and a quantitative Fourier-smoothing mechanism supply more than a known-moment re-expression or an arbitrary numerical slice; the result is a natural structural limit for the model.
